title: vLLM audio transcription -- T1499 compressed-size limit ignores decoded PCM expansion
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54233 (GHSA-6pr9-rp53-2pmc,
CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM), affecting vLLM prior to 0.23.1rc0.

`/v1/audio/transcriptions` limits the COMPRESSED upload size but never
bounds the DECODED PCM output size -- a classic decompression-bomb
shape. The advisory's own measured ratio: a 25MB OPUS file (within the
compressed limit) expands to approximately 14.9GB of float32 PCM at
decode time. A caller submitting an ordinary, size-compliant compressed
audio file can therefore still cause the server to allocate gigabytes
of decoded audio data, exhausting memory regardless of the compressed
upload staying comfortably under the documented limit -- the same
outcome as `observed_vllm_audio_upload_pre_limit_memory_exhaustion_t1499`
(buffer-before-check), but reached through a completely different
mechanism: high compression ratio rather than a missing check ordering.

Detection logic flags an audio-transcription upload using a
high-compression-ratio codec (OPUS, or other codecs with similarly
extreme compressed:decoded ratios) at or near the compressed-size
limit -- since the vulnerable code path bounds only the compressed
size, a request maximizing that size while using a high-ratio codec is
the specific shape that triggers the largest possible decoded
allocation.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (vllm-project,
via GHSA and NVD, citing the exact fix PR and the measured 25MB->14.9GB
expansion ratio), fixed in 0.23.1rc0.
